name: Rabbit Meat
imageAlt: fresh raw lean rabbit meat portions on a clean light slate surface
description: Rabbit meat is an elite, ultra-lean white meat derived from Oryctolagus cuniculus. Globally recognized for its exceptional structural density, minimal lipid footprint, and high biological value, it stands as one of the most allergen-friendly, easily digestible mammalian proteins available. Rich in intracellular electrolytes and essential B-complex cofactors, it provides premium metabolic support for cardiovascular integrity and deep myofibrillar synthesis.
macroIntro: Rabbit meat exhibits a highly efficient, protein-dominant macronutrient profile, yielding an exceptionally low caloric weight alongside minimal saturated lipid levels.
microIntro: Rabbit meat features an advanced, highly bioavailable micronutrient matrix, offering massive thresholds of intracellular potassium, metabolic phosphorus, and neural B-complex vitamins.

precautionsIntro: Purine Nucleotide Base Load, High-Protein Malnutrition Risk (Rabbit Starvation), and Thermal Processing Guidelines: Calibrated integration ensures balanced metabolic parameters.
precautions: Purine Nucleotide Accumulation Risks: Rabbit meat houses moderate concentrations of natural purines. Excess metabolic breakdown can elevate serum uric acid levels, necessitating portion control for individuals prone to gout.

Lean Protein Malnutrition Limitations: Due to the extreme absence of fat mass, relying exclusively on rabbit meat as a singular macro source without supplemental dietary fats can disrupt nitrogen-to-lipid metabolic balancing (known historically as rabbit starvation).

Oxidative Degradation Overcooking Hazards: Because of its ultra-lean tissue architecture, rapid exposure to high-temperature dry cooking can cause immediate moisture evacuation, necessitating gentle, moisture-rich culinary processing to avoid tough myofibrils.
